title: Making The Leap: why Corey Haines went full-time creator and the stairstep path to bootstrapping
summary: Corey explains why he left Baremetrics to go full time on his own work. He covers timing the leap before kids and a mortgage, following Rob Walling's stairstep approach to bootstrapping, and using regret minimization and intrinsic motivation (autonomy, mastery, purpose) to make the call.

principles.text: Take the entrepreneurial leap before kids and a mortgage, when the downside is a few months of savings.
principles.quote: I’d rather risk a few months of savings than my house or ability to put food on the table for my kids. Not impossible, but I’d rather play on “easy mode” if I can help it.

principles.text: Bootstrap by climbing the stairstep: start with small products and work up to harder businesses like SaaS.
principles.quote: I’ve loosely followed Rob Walling’s “stairstep approach to bootstrapping" which describes taking entrepreneurship one step at a time, each a bit more difficult and rewarding as the last.

principles.text: Fund your runway with light consulting while you build your own product toward a bootstrapped SaaS.
principles.quote: Right now, I plan to keep afloat with some light consulting while I work on building up Swipe Files to pay my bills. The eventual goal is to bootstrap a B2B SaaS company.

principles.text: Entrepreneurs are ordinary people who take initiative to make something exist that they wish existed.
principles.quote: Entrepreneurs are just normal people who take initiative. And if I wanted to bring something into existence, I could. There’s nothing stopping me.

principles.text: Use regret minimization to make big career decisions: ask whether you'll regret not doing it in X years.
principles.quote: When I ask myself, “In X years, will I regret not doing this?” the answer is an unequivocal and resounding YES.

principles.text: Build around intrinsic motivation (autonomy, mastery, purpose) rather than money, status or titles.
principles.quote: I’m just not that motivated by extrinsic rewards—money, status, titles, recognition. Intrinsic rewards—autonomy, mastery, purpose—are what drive me.
